Subject: POC kickoff & workshop scheduling for Acme Health

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Hope you're well. We'd like to kick off the POC for Acme Health and schedule a hands-on workshop where we can:
- Review and iterate on prompt sets
- Discuss routing and failover behavior for our clinical workflows
- Run lightweight load tests and validate latency under expected traffic

We are trying to decide whether to host this onsite at our HQ (San Francisco) or do a virtual workshop. Our preferences: onsite if possible (we'd like to have a working session with screen sharing, access to our network for load tests, and the option to record for the internal team), but virtual works if there are security or logistics blockers.

Possible windows: week of Mar 23 (preferred) or Mar 30 as a backup. Ideal session length is a half-day (3-4 hours) with two blocks: prompt review & routing (90 mins) then load tests & tuning (90-120 mins).

Can you confirm availability the week of Mar 23 and any requirements for visitor access / AV / recording permissions? Also please share a draft agenda and any pre-reqs for network access if we're doing load tests on-prem.

Thanks,
Anna

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the options. Quick updates from our side:
- Our stakeholders prefer onsite and Mar 25 (Wed) morning would work best for the team here (we can do a 09:00-13:00 block).
- Facilities will need a room spec: capacity ~12, HDMI + laptop support, Zoom room for remote attendees, and recording capability (we'd like the session recorded for internal review).
- Visitor access: we need to pre-register guests for building pass and sign NDA at reception. I'll share the attendee list once you confirm.

Procurement is cc'd — they may need to confirm the SOW and timing for the reserved testing window.

Hi all,

Quick technical note ahead of the workshop:
- Load test ramp plan (attached): we recommend a 3-step ramp (baseline, +50% concurrent, peak). Total test window ~20 mins per run; plan for two runs back-to-back with a 10-min cool-down.
- Data: please confirm whether we should use synthetic payloads or a de-identified sample. If using a de-identified sample we'll need a short Data Access Agreement and confirmation from Acme security.
- Network: if testing on Acme network, we need the IP allowlist for our test harness (I'll provide the exact IPs). If not possible, we'll use our dedicated test env and capture comparative telemetry (latency, p95, memory).
- Permissions: to record the meeting and capture logs we'll need written confirmation of where recordings/logs can be stored (Redwood cloud vs. Acme internal storage).

Attachment: [load_test_plan.pdf]

I'll be on-site if the session is in SF — happy to coordinate the AV checks 30 minutes prior.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
